hypothesis: A large daily move in the 10y Treasury yield at the prior close reprices equities with a lag, so the next ES RTH session moves against the yield change (yields up -> ES down); trading 09:35 -> 15:55 on -sign(z) beats side-matched random twins.
mechanism: Discount-rate shocks are absorbed slowly by equity investors (cross-asset information diffusion, slow-moving capital): the equity response to a rate shock is spread over the following session.
overlap_with_closed: Not on research_loop/CLOSED_IDEAS.md. D2 used Δ10y only inside a month-end equity-minus-bond composite on the last 3-5 sessions of a month; V3 used the VIX term structure. This conditions on the prior day's yield change alone, every session.
timestamp_semantics: hist[-1].ust10y is the Treasury par yield dated the previous ES session (published after the bond close that day), known at today's 09:30. Δ10y(prev) = hist[-1].ust10y - hist[-2].ust10y; None if either is None (bond-market holiday) -> no trade.

rules.z: z = Δ10y(prev) / sd, sd = sample sd of the consecutive-session Δ10y values inside bar['hist'] (up to 60 sessions -> up to 59 deltas, pairs with a None yield skipped), requiring >= 40 valid deltas and sd > 0.
rules.entry_exit: evaluator trade shape: decided on the 09:30 bar, market at the 09:35 open, 1:1 bracket of k x ATR20(tr) around the 09:30 close, flat 15:55 (12:55 half days). One trade per session.

expected_sign: positive mean net R; Z = 2 at least as strong as Z = 1.
against_the_mechanism: The sign flips by era: report net R per dev year. Dev 2011-18 lies entirely in the negative stock-bond return correlation era; if the effect is mixed in sign across years (fewer than 6 of 8 years with the expected sign at Z=1), the mechanism is not stable.
Z = 2 weaker (lower mean net R) than Z = 1: larger shocks should matter more.
Report only: the same-direction split (yields up days vs yields down days); a one-sided effect is a long/short drift artefact (side-matched twins already control the average side).
The frozen dev gate failing for all Z.
expected_trades: |z| >= 1 ~ 30% of ~1,980 dev sessions (~600); |z| >= 2 ~ 5% (~100, likely under the 200-trade floor). No config is dropped or replaced.
walk_forward: none; inherited dev gate incl. neighbour positivity; a pass freezes that config for one val1 look.
